text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Council of State documents, which went missing from the president's palace, may have been sent to the offices of the Revolution Council, an adviser to the Revolution Council Vasco Lourenco told the paper. An investigation is under way into the whereabouts of the documents.
- Champalimaud group banks Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor and Banco Totta & Acores dominated activity on Lisbon stock exchange yesterday.
- Second occupation of the Portuguese consulate in Vigo, Galicia in two weeks by dozens of workers dismissed by Ormis, a company based in Galicia that has Portuguese financial backing.

- Portugal's biggest state bank Caixa Geral de Depositos (CGD) and IPE-Investimento e Participacoes Empresarias paid around 11 billion escudos for a 10 percent stake in motorway company Brisa which belonged to French company Eiffage.

- The board of Empresa do Metro do Porto has chosen two international consortia led by German group Siemens and Portuguese group Soares da Costa as finalists in the public competition to build a 130 billion escudos urban transport system in Oporto, officials said. The two finalists were chosen from four consortia.
- Construction company Engil said it forsaw 1997 profits of between 1.72 and 1.75 billion escudos and turnover no less than 70 billion escudos, a statement from the company said.
